title: Flydubai Partners Air India, Uzbekistan Airways to Add 80 Destinations
excerpt: The Dubai-based carrier's new interline agreements give its passengers single-ticket access to more than 80 additional destinations across Asia, Australia and Europe, taking its partner network to 46 airlines and its combined reach past 300 destinations worldwide.
body:
• Flydubai announced new interline agreements with Air India and Uzbekistan Airways on September 16, 2026, opening access to more than 80 additional destinations across Asia, Australia and Europe.
  • Passengers can combine flights on single-ticket itineraries with baggage checked through to their final destination, connecting through Dubai and Tashkent.
  • The deals take flydubai's interline network to 46 partner airlines, with combined interline and codeshare reach now exceeding 300 destinations worldwide.
  • Through Air India, flydubai passengers gain access to Indian cities including Bengaluru, Chennai, Chandigarh, Goa, Jaipur, Pune and Varanasi, plus gateways like Sydney, Melbourne, Singapore, Tokyo and Hong Kong.

DUBAI — Dubai-based carrier flydubai has signed interline agreements with Air India and Uzbekistan Airways, adding more than 80 destinations to its network and giving its passengers single-ticket access across Asia, Australia and Europe, the airline announced on Wednesday.

The partnerships let travellers combine flights operated by the airlines on one ticket, with baggage checked through to the final destination. Air India and Uzbekistan Airways passengers, in turn, gain convenient connections to flydubai's network via Dubai. With the additions, flydubai's interline network now comprises 46 partner airlines, reinforcing its role in Dubai's position as a global hub for travel and commerce.

What the Air India Link Opens Up

Through Air India, flydubai customers gain access to Indian destinations including Bengaluru, Chennai, Chandigarh, Goa, Jaipur, Pune and Varanasi — several of them tier-two cities that lack direct links to the Gulf. Internationally, the agreement opens gateways including Bali, Ho Chi Minh City, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Mauritius, Melbourne, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney and Tokyo.

Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer at Air India, said the airline is steadily expanding partnerships with leading carriers worldwide to offer customers wider network access, and that the tie-up improves access to Middle East markets via Dubai while bringing flydubai customers onto Air India's expanding international network.

The Central Asia Corridor

The Uzbekistan Airways agreement routes connections through Tashkent. Passengers can reach Russian cities including Irkutsk, Krasnoyarsk and Moscow, major European gateways such as Frankfurt, London, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome, and Uzbek destinations including Bukhara, Fergana and Urgench.

Shukhrat Khudaykulov, chairman of the board of Uzbekistan Airways, said the cooperation combines the strengths of both airlines' route networks and provides passengers with more international travel options.

"Our interline partnerships with Air India and Uzbekistan Airways mark a significant step forward in flydubai's network expansion strategy, offering our passengers greater choice as they connect through Dubai. Air India brings South Asia, Southeast Asia and Australian markets within reach, while Uzbekistan Airways adds a vital corridor through Central Asia, Russia and into Europe."

— Ghaith Al Ghaith, Chief Executive Officer, flydubai

Context: A Decade of Route Building

Flydubai, which began operations in 2009, has built a network covering more than 120 destinations and says it has opened more than 100 routes to markets that previously had no direct air links to Dubai or were not served by a UAE national carrier. Its interline and codeshare arrangements now provide access to more than 300 destinations worldwide. Passengers connecting onto flydubai flights fly its Boeing 737 fleet, with lie-flat seats in Business Class and ergonomic seating, complimentary dining and inflight entertainment in Economy.

Interline journeys involving Air India and Uzbekistan Airways are available to book through flydubai's website and app, the partner airlines' websites, its contact centre, travel shops and travel partners.

The Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the practical payoff is routing flexibility. Millions of Indians in the Gulf, the US and Australia travel to India via Dubai each year, and the new single-ticket access extends beyond metros like Bengaluru and Chennai into cities such as Jaipur, Pune, Chandigarh and Varanasi — home bases for many NRI families that today require an extra domestic connection. Through-checked baggage and one itinerary also mean fewer missed-connection risks on the multi-leg journeys that define diaspora travel.

What's Next

The deals are bookable now across flydubai's sales channels. Watch for how quickly the interline fares show up in aggregators for routes like Dubai–Sydney or Dubai–Tokyo via Air India, and whether flydubai continues its run of partner announcements — 46 and counting — through the rest of the year.
